bounds: One turn of the opt-in secret swap with one session: two character secrets the session numbers when it is created, one phone number the user types (numbered when a prompt first shows it) and one reference with the session's nonce and an index the session never numbers. A model call shows any non-empty set of the first three values; after the model has seen one reference it may write any of the four references into an action argument, and the planner may execute that call or stop. The conformance script replays every generated sequence on a real AgentRuntime with ELIZA_SECRET_SWAP_ENABLED: prompts go through useModel and its secret swap, action calls through executePlannedToolCall, and it requires each of the seven (reference, shown or not) outcomes that the bounds allow. Environment-derived secrets, PII pseudonyms, streaming, reply restoration and concurrent turns are not modeled. Under weak fairness of execution a planned call is eventually executed or rejected; explicit stuttering lets the planner stop, so the same claim without fairness must fail. No time bound is proved.

assumptions: A continuously enabled execution of the planned call eventually happens (weak fairness). This checks that the boundary then either restores the reference or rejects the call, not how long the planner takes.
No execution fairness is assumed. The planner may stop before it executes the call, so a temporal loop counterexample is required.
